title: Powers of Ten — Nested Scale Traverse
subtitle: Order-of-magnitude steps from human hand (10^-1 m) to cosmos (10^6 m) and back to cells
lineage: Lineage: Charles & Ray Eames, Powers of Ten (1977) · Kees Boeke (1957)
theorem: Move across orders of magnitude at a steady declared cadence so the viewer perceives how pattern and organization alternate with vast intervals across human, urban, planetary, and microscopic scales.
boundary_note: Archive shots from different films are linked by explicit order-of-magnitude scale brackets (`10^-1 m` to `10^6 m` and `10^-4 m`) rather than claiming a continuous optical zoom of one location.

critic_tribunal.largest_gap: Uses `reframe` and verified scale shots from `1570ec0b` (hand skin 10^-1 m) through `46cd8d58` (garden chair 10^0 m), `6eb03e7f` (intersection 10^2 m), `cf5b2845` (town aerial 10^3 m), `c1ba4a8c` (shoreline 10^5 m), `201b010b` (star field), and back to `efedc39b` / `64a0a6c1` (microscopy 10^-4 m).
critic_tribunal.falsifiable_repair: All 8 scale brackets use human-verified Cineosis shots with cut-free windows.
